source_passages.section: Actions — Shared movement, crafting and battle
source_passages.quotation: Clearings have fox, rabbit or mouse suit and limited building slots. Buildings require open slots; tokens do not occupy these. Ruins block their slots and can be removed only when explicitly allowed. A forest is enclosed by printed paths and clearings; it is adjacent to clearings touching it without crossing a printed path and to forests separated by just one printed path. Winter's river also divides forests. (2.2–2.4, M.1–2.)

answer.ruling: A clearing is ruled by the player with more total warriors plus buildings than each other player. Tokens and pawns do not count. Ordinary ties mean no one rules; Eyrie break a tie for most if they have at least one Eyrie piece there. Vagabond cannot rule or prevent another player from ruling.

source_passages.quotation: **Craft (4.1):** **Every crafting piece gets its suit from the clearing containing it.** The card's **bottom-left crafting icons** require pieces of those clearing suits; the card's own suit does not define the cost. Craft a card from hand when your faction permits.

answer.ruling: Move any positive number of your warriors or pawns from one clearing along a linking path to an adjacent clearing. You must rule the origin or destination or both, and recheck rule for each move. You may move the same pieces repeatedly, including on multiple moves in one action. Rivers are not paths unless an effect explicitly treats them as paths. Vagabond movement has its own exceptions.

| Immediate-effect crafting card | Your hand | Shared discard pile after resolving |
| Persistent-effect crafting card | Your hand | Your play area |
| Item token produced by an item card | Map item supply | Crafting faction’s Crafted Items box; when Vagabond itself crafts, it may immediately take its crafted item face up into Satchel/track |

- Persistent effect (stone box): keep card in your play area and gain its text, subject to the personal duplicate check above. Its card is outside your hand and cannot be spent/discarded/used for another purpose unless explicitly instructed.
- **Ambush cards cannot be crafted:** the defender may play one for two immediate hits, or the attacker may play one to foil a defending ambush, matching the clearing. **Dominance cards cannot be crafted:** activate one to change victory condition, or spend it for suit.

**Battle (4.3):** Choose a clearing with your warriors or pawn and an enemy there as defender. **Battle does not require you to rule the clearing.** Resolve these six steps:

answer.ruling: Choose a clearing with your warriors or pawn and an enemy as defender; ruling is not required. Resolve: (1) defender may play a matching ambush (birds wild); attacker may foil with matching ambush. Defender discards it; if foiled it deals no hits, otherwise it deals two immediate hits and is discarded. If no attacking warriors or pawns remain, battle ends immediately. Ambush hits are not capped by defending warriors. (2) Resolve before-roll effects; attacker chooses order if both players have them. (3) Roll: higher die is attacker hits and lower is defender hits; ties give equal results. Each side caps rolled hits by its own warriors in battle; Alliance defending reverses dice, and Vagabond uses undamaged swords instead of warriors. (4) Resolve after-roll effects; attacker chooses order if both players have them. (5) Add extra hits (not capped by warriors), subtract ignored hits; if defender has no warriors, attacker gets one defenseless extra hit, except Vagabond is defenseless only if it has no undamaged swords. (6) Each hit removes one opposing piece; hit-taking side chooses its removal order but must remove all warriors before buildings/tokens, and chooses order of effects triggered by its pieces’ removal. Both sides deal counted hits even if warriors were lost after the roll. Removing an enemy building or token scores one VP each, even while defending and outside battle. Vagabond takes hits as item damage instead.

source_passages.quotation:
**Personal duplicate check:** Only an identical persistent effect **in your own play area** prevents you from crafting that effect again. Other players' copies do not count for this duplicate restriction.

- **Marquise, Eyrie and Alliance cost:** For **each icon**, activate **one workshop, roost or sympathy in a clearing matching that icon's suit**, respectively. A crafting piece gets its suit from its clearing. Combine eligible pieces as needed, but **each piece may activate only once per turn**.
- **Vagabond cost and reuse:** The pawn **may activate repeatedly in a turn**. For each icon, **pay by exhausting one face-up, undamaged hammer: flip that hammer face down**. The pawn's **current clearing must match every icon on the card**. Reusing the pawn never waives the hammer payment per icon. One clearing cannot pay mixed fox/rabbit/mouse icons.
- A **three-color question-mark icon** accepts any suit.

- Immediate effect (paper box): resolve, then discard the **crafting card**. An item card requires the corresponding **item token** in the map supply, or it cannot be crafted. Take the item token into Crafted Items and score the VP printed on the card, subject to Eyrie exception. The item token stays; the crafting card is discarded. Ordinary factions do not exhaust crafted items as Vagabond does.

| Separate component after a successful craft | Starts in | Goes to |

answer.part: Crafting cost, reuse, supply and duplicate check
answer.ruling: Craft from hand when your faction permits. Each crafting piece gets its suit from its clearing; a card’s bottom-left crafting icons require pieces of those suits, not the card’s suit. For Marquise, Eyrie and Alliance, each icon uses one workshop, roost or sympathy respectively in a clearing matching that icon; eligible pieces may be combined, but each piece activates only once per turn. Vagabond may reuse its pawn in a turn, but pays each icon by flipping one face-up, undamaged hammer face down; the pawn’s current clearing must match every icon, so one clearing cannot pay mixed suits. A three-color question-mark accepts any suit. An item card cannot be crafted without its corresponding item token in map supply. Only an identical persistent effect in your own play area prevents crafting it again; another player’s copy does not.

**Dominance (3.3):** In own Daylight at **at least 10 VP**, activate a dominance card from hand into play area; remove score marker and stop scoring VP. Cannot remove/replace activated card. At **start of own Birdsong**, win if ruling **three clearings of matching mouse/rabbit/fox suit**, or for **bird dominance, two diagonally opposite corner clearings**. Meeting condition earlier does not immediately win. Dominance cards cannot be crafted, but can be spent for suit. Whenever one would enter discard, put it near map available instead. During own Daylight, spend matching card to take available dominance into hand. Available **bird dominance remains bird**, so payment must be bird; a bird hand card can pay for non-bird dominance. Activation and taking are separate, neither requires a faction action allowance.

answer.ruling: During your own Daylight, at at least 10 VP, activate a dominance card from hand into your play area; remove your score marker and stop scoring VP.

answer.part: Win conditions by suit and replacement/discard
answer.ruling: At the start of your own Birdsong, mouse/rabbit/fox dominance wins if you rule three clearings of that suit; bird dominance wins if you rule two diagonally opposite corner clearings. Satisfying the condition earlier does not win immediately. You cannot remove or replace an activated card.

source_passages.quotation: **Dominance (3.3):** In own Daylight at **at least 10 VP**, activate a dominance card from hand into play area; remove score marker and stop scoring VP. Cannot remove/replace activated card. At **start of own Birdsong**, win if ruling **three clearings of matching mouse/rabbit/fox suit**, or for **bird dominance, two diagonally opposite corner clearings**. Meeting condition earlier does not immediately win. Dominance cards cannot be crafted, but can be spent for suit. Whenever one would enter discard, put it near map available instead. During own Daylight, spend matching card to take available dominance into hand. Available **bird dominance remains bird**, so payment must be bird; a bird hand card can pay for non-bird dominance. Activation and taking are separate, neither requires a faction action allowance.

answer.ruling: When a dominance card would enter discard, put it near the map as available. During your own Daylight, spend a matching card to take an available dominance card into hand. An available bird dominance remains bird, so its payment must be a bird; a bird card can pay for a non-bird dominance. Taking it does not activate it, and neither taking nor activation uses a faction action allowance.

source_passages.quotation:
1. Choose factions; determine starting player and seating randomly. Take faction boards and their listed pieces. Use Fall or Winter. Fall has no special rules; on Winter, the river divides forests just as printed paths do. Rivers are otherwise not paths.
2. Put score markers at 0.
3. With two players, remove all four dominance cards. Shuffle shared deck; each player draws **three cards**.
4. **Ruins and items:** Cover the four R building slots with ruins. The separate map item supply is **2 boots, 2 bags, 1 crossbow, 1 hammer, 2 swords, 2 tea, 2 coins**. Keep the four R-marked ruin items separate from this supply: only Vagabond faction setup hides one each of its R-marked bag, boot, hammer and sword beneath the four ruins, **one item beneath each ruin**. During that Vagabond setup, shuffle the ruin/item stacks and return each to an empty R ruin slot, keeping item identities hidden. Without a Vagabond, ruins contain no items.
5. The map item supply uses its corresponding spaces near the top of the map.
6. Distribute overview cards as desired; put battle dice nearby.
7. Set up factions in their letter order: Marquise, Eyrie, Alliance, Vagabond. Setup order is distinct from turn order.

**Hidden ruin items (only when Vagabond is present, during its faction setup):**

1. Take the four ruins and R-marked bag, boot, hammer and sword. Put **one item beneath each ruin**.
2. **Shuffle the ruin/item stacks**, keeping identities hidden.
3. **Return each stack to an empty R ruin slot** on the map. With no Vagabond, leave the four ruins without hidden items.

answer.part: Two-player deck, hand, ruins and map items
answer.ruling: In standard setup, determine starting player and seating randomly; put score markers at zero. With two players, remove all four dominance cards, shuffle the shared deck, and each player draws three cards. Cover the four R building slots with ruins. The separate map item supply is 2 boots, 2 bags, 1 crossbow, 1 hammer, 2 swords, 2 tea and 2 coins, using corresponding map spaces. Only when Vagabond is present, during its faction setup, put one R-marked bag, boot, hammer and sword beneath the four ruins, one under each; shuffle the ruin/item stacks while keeping identities hidden, then return each to an empty R slot. Without Vagabond, leave ruins without hidden items.
Set up factions in letter order: Marquise, Eyrie, Alliance, Vagabond. This setup order is distinct from turn order.

source_passages.section: Marquise de Cat — Keep and Field Hospitals
source_passages.quotation: **Keep:** Only Marquise may **place** pieces in its clearing; other players may **move** pieces into it. The keep cannot be placed again if removed. **Field Hospitals:** Whenever any number of Marquise warriors are removed from a clearing, Marquise may spend one card matching that clearing to place those warriors in the keep clearing instead of supply. This can apply outside battle. Without a keep there is no destination for hospitals. See **FAQ & Rulings** for Hospitals during an ambush at the Keep.

source_passages.section: FAQ & Rulings — Field Hospitals during an ambush at the Keep
source_passages.quotation: - **Field Hospitals during an ambush at the Keep:** Marquise may spend a matching card immediately when its warriors are removed, returning them to the Keep clearing **before** checking whether the ambush left no attacking warriors or pawns. If returned warriors remain there, battle continues. Without Hospitals, battle ends if no attackers remain after the ambush. (FAQ under 4.3.1 and 6.2.3.)

answer.ruling: Only Marquise may place pieces in the Keep clearing; other players may move pieces into it. If the Keep is removed, it cannot be placed again.
answer.evidence: Marquise de Cat — Keep and Field Hospitals

answer.ruling: Whenever any number of Marquise warriors are removed from a clearing, Marquise may spend one card matching that clearing to put those warriors in the Keep clearing instead of supply; this can happen outside battle. There is no Hospitals destination without a Keep. During an ambush at the Keep, Marquise may spend the matching card immediately as warriors are removed, returning them before checking whether no attackers remain. If returned warriors remain there, battle continues; without Hospitals, battle ends if the ambush leaves no attackers.

source_passages.quotation:
**Daylight:** First craft with workshops. Then take **up to three actions**, plus **one per bird card spent outside an action**, in any order and number except Recruit's limit:

- **Battle:** One battle.
- **March:** Up to two moves; either may use the same or different warriors. Do not interrupt the compound action to spend a bird card or take another action.
- **Recruit:** One warrior at **each recruiter**; only **once per turn**. If supply cannot fill all recruiters, place maximum available, choosing among eligible recruiters.
- **Build:** Choose a clearing you rule with open slot and choose building type. Take the leftmost building of that type. Pay cost shown atop its column by removing that many wood from the target clearing or from other ruled clearings linked to it through an unbroken chain of ruled clearings. Place building; score VP on uncovered space. You cannot build without full wood cost, the building and legal slot.
- **Overwork:** Spend a card matching a sawmill's clearing to place one wood there.

answer.ruling: First craft with workshops. Then take up to three actions, plus one action for each bird card spent outside an action. Actions may be taken in any order and number, subject to Recruit’s limit.

March is up to two moves; the moves may use the same or different warriors and cannot be interrupted to spend a bird card or take another action. Recruit places one warrior at each recruiter and is allowed only once per turn; if supply cannot fill all recruiters, place the maximum available, choosing among eligible recruiters. Overwork spends a card matching a sawmill’s clearing to place one wood there.

source_passages.quotation: - **Build:** Choose a clearing you rule with open slot and choose building type. Take the leftmost building of that type. Pay cost shown atop its column by removing that many wood from the target clearing or from other ruled clearings linked to it through an unbroken chain of ruled clearings. Place building; score VP on uncovered space. You cannot build without full wood cost, the building and legal slot.

answer.part: Build eligibility, cost, piece and scoring
answer.ruling: Choose a clearing you rule with an open building slot and choose a building type. Take the leftmost building of that type. Pay the column cost by removing that many wood from the target clearing or from other ruled clearings connected to it through an unbroken chain of ruled clearings. Place the building and score the VP on the newly uncovered space. Building is not allowed unless the full wood cost, building and legal slot are available.

source_passages.quotation:
**Birdsong, in order:**

1. **Emergency Orders:** If hand empty, draw one.
2. **Add to Decree:** Must add one or two hand cards, **at most one added bird card**. Each goes to any column; columns have no size limit.
3. **A New Roost:** If no roosts on map, place one roost and three warriors in a clearing with the fewest warriors **where all these pieces can be placed**.

answer.part: Emergency Orders and adding to Decree
answer.ruling: In Birdsong, first draw one card if your hand is empty. Then add one or two cards from hand to any Decree columns; at most one may be a bird, and columns have no size limit.
If there are no roosts on the map, place one roost and three warriors in a clearing with the fewest warriors where all four pieces can be placed.

source_passages.quotation:
**Daylight — resolve the Decree:** Craft using roosts first, then resolve **every Decree card**, column by column **Recruit → Move → Battle → Build**. Within one column choose card order freely. Bird is wild. **If any required action cannot be fully completed, immediately enter Turmoil: you cannot skip the card or continue other columns.** For a prompted placement with too few pieces, first place the maximum possible, then enter Turmoil because the action remains incomplete (publisher clarification in **FAQ & Rulings**). Each card requires:

| Decree column | Match the card's suit to | Required procedure for one card |
|---|---|---|
| Recruit | Clearing with a roost | Place **one warrior at one chosen roost** there; Charismatic must instead place **two warriors** there |
| Move | Origin clearing | Move **at least one warrior**, obeying ordinary path and rule requirements |
| Battle | Clearing of battle | Initiate a battle there with Eyrie warriors and an enemy |
| Build | Target clearing | Place one roost in a clearing you rule, with an open slot and **no roost already there** |

**Bird Decree cards are wild in every column:** choose any clearing suit, while still meeting that action’s other requirements.

answer.part: Decree order, suit locations and action requirements
answer.ruling: Craft with roosts first, then resolve every Decree card in column order Recruit, Move, Battle, Build. Within a column, choose card order freely. A card must match the clearing suit as follows: Recruit matches a clearing with a roost and places one warrior at one chosen roost there (Charismatic places two); Move matches the origin and moves at least one warrior under normal path and rule rules; Battle matches the battle clearing and initiates a battle there with Eyrie warriors and an enemy; Build matches the target and places one roost in a clearing you rule with an open slot and no roost already there. Bird cards are wild in every column, but all other action requirements still apply. Each Decree action must be fully completed or Turmoil starts immediately; the card cannot be skipped and other columns cannot continue. If placement supply is short, place the maximum possible first, then enter Turmoil for the incomplete action.

source_passages.quotation:
**Turmoil, in order:** Lose one VP per bird Decree card **including both Loyal Viziers**; discard every Decree card except Viziers; flip current leader face down and choose a face-up replacement. If none face up, flip all leaders face up before choosing. Retuck Viziers in new leader's columns. End Daylight and proceed to the full normal Evening: **score the roost track, draw one plus uncovered bonuses, then discard to five**. **Turmoil does not remove your map warriors or buildings.**

**Evening, even after turmoil:** Score the VP on rightmost empty roost-track space. Draw one plus uncovered draw bonuses; discard down to five.

answer.part: Turmoil sequence and rest of turn
answer.ruling: Lose one VP for each bird Decree card, including both Loyal Viziers; discard every Decree card except Viziers; flip the current leader face down and choose a face-up replacement, flipping all leaders face up first if none are face up; retuck Viziers in the new leader’s columns. Daylight ends and normal Evening follows: score the roost track, draw one card plus uncovered bonuses, then discard to five. Turmoil does not remove map warriors or buildings. In an ordinary Evening, score the VP on the rightmost empty roost-track space, draw one plus uncovered draw bonuses, and discard down to five; scoring/drawing/discard still happen after Turmoil.

source_passages.quotation: **Outrage:** Each time another player **removes sympathy** or **moves any warriors into a sympathetic clearing**, that player adds one matching hand card (birds count) to Supporters. Moving a group costs one card per affected move, rather than one per warrior. If no matching cards including birds, show hand to Alliance, then Alliance draws one deck card into Supporters. **If Supporters is full, discard the incoming Outrage card; payment or the no-match draw still occurs.** Merely battling there is no trigger unless sympathy is removed; placing warriors there and moving only Vagabond pawn do not trigger it.

answer.ruling: Outrage triggers when another player removes sympathy or moves any warriors into a sympathetic clearing. That player adds one matching card from hand to Supporters (birds count), once per affected move rather than per warrior in a group. Merely battling there is not a trigger unless sympathy is removed; placing warriors there and moving only the Vagabond pawn do not trigger it.

answer.part: No matching card and full Supporters stack
answer.ruling: If the player has no matching card, including birds, they show their hand to the Alliance, then the Alliance draws one deck card into Supporters. If Supporters is full, the incoming Outrage card is discarded; the payment or no-match draw still happens.

source_passages.section: Woodland Alliance — Birdsong Revolt and Spread Sympathy
source_passages.quotation:
**Birdsong:** Both Revolt and Spread Sympathy take place **during Birdsong**. Complete **all Revolts before starting any Spread Sympathy**; each may be performed any number of times. **For both actions, every supporter spent must match the target clearing; birds are wild.** Once spreading starts, you cannot return to Revolt this Birdsong, so newly spread sympathy cannot support a same-Birdsong Revolt:

- **Revolt:** Choose sympathetic clearing without a base, matching a base still on your board. Spend **two matching supporters**. **Remove all enemy pieces there and score one VP per enemy building/token removed**; then place matching base. Place warriors there equal to number of sympathetic clearings matching the base's printed suit (including revolt clearing), and one warrior in Officers box. Score normal VP for removed enemy buildings/tokens. Resolve the effect even if a prompted placement cannot be completed: place the maximum possible, without adding a base-placement prerequisite. Enemy Vagabond damages three items instead of being removed.
- **Spread Sympathy:** Choose unsympathetic clearing adjacent by path to sympathy; if no sympathy anywhere, choose any clearing. Spend matching supporters shown above next sympathy token. **Martial Law:** add one matching supporter if chosen clearing has at least three warriors of **one other player**. Place token and score uncovered space. Only one sympathy per clearing. Keep's placement ban still applies.

answer.part: Timing, order and shared supporter suit
answer.ruling: Revolt and Spread Sympathy both occur during Birdsong. Complete all Revolts before starting Spread Sympathy; either action may be performed any number of times. Every supporter spent for either action must match the target clearing, with birds wild. Once spreading starts, Revolt cannot resume that Birdsong, so new sympathy cannot fund a same-Birdsong Revolt.
answer.evidence: Woodland Alliance — Birdsong Revolt and Spread Sympathy

answer.ruling: Choose a sympathetic clearing without a base that matches a base still on your board. Spend two matching supporters. Remove all enemy pieces there, scoring one VP per enemy building or token removed, then place the matching base. Place warriors there equal to the number of sympathetic clearings matching that base’s printed suit, including the revolt clearing, and one warrior in the Officers box. Score normal VP for enemy buildings/tokens removed. If a prompted placement is short, place the maximum possible; this does not add a base-placement prerequisite. An enemy Vagabond damages three items instead of being removed.
answer.evidence: Woodland Alliance — Birdsong Revolt and Spread Sympathy

answer.part: Spread Sympathy eligibility, cost, Martial Law and result
answer.ruling: Choose an unsympathetic clearing adjacent by path to sympathy, or any clearing if there is no sympathy anywhere. Spend the number of supporters shown above the next sympathy token, matching that target clearing. If the chosen clearing has at least three warriors of one other player, Martial Law adds one matching supporter. Place the sympathy token and score the uncovered VP space. Only one sympathy token is allowed per clearing, and the Keep’s placement ban remains.
answer.evidence: Woodland Alliance — Birdsong Revolt and Spread Sympathy

evidence: Woodland Alliance — Birdsong Revolt and Spread Sympathy

source_passages.quotation: **Losing a base:** Discard all supporters matching its clearing **including birds**, remove half officers **rounded up**. If no bases remain, discard excess supporters down to five. Do this whenever a base is removed.

source_passages.section: Woodland Alliance — Daylight and Evening operations
source_passages.quotation:
**Daylight:** Any order and number:

- **Craft** from hand with sympathy.
- **Mobilize:** Add one hand card to Supporters. With no base on map, keep at most five supporters and discard incoming overflow; with any base, the stack has no cap.
- **Train during Daylight:** Spend a **hand card** matching a clearing with a base to place one supply warrior in Officers box. Supporters cannot pay Train. Each officer allows one Evening military operation; taking operations does not consume officers.

**Evening:** The four military operations are **Move, Battle, Recruit and Organize**. Take **up to your number of officers** in operations, in any order and repetition. Officers stay on the board; taking an operation does not consume an officer. After operations, draw one card plus one per uncovered draw bonus, then discard hand down to five.

| Military operation | Procedure for one operation |
|---|---|
| Move | Take one move using normal movement rules |
| Battle | Initiate one battle |
| Recruit | Place one warrior at one clearing with a base |
| Organize | Remove one Alliance warrior from an unsympathetic clearing; place sympathy there; score the uncovered VP |

Organize spends no supporters and has no sympathy-adjacency requirement or Martial Law cost; it still needs legal token placement. **After operations**, draw one card plus one per uncovered draw bonus, then discard hand down to five.

answer.ruling: During Daylight, spend a hand card matching a clearing with a base to place one warrior from supply into the Officers box. Supporters cannot pay Train. Each officer permits one Evening military operation; taking operations does not consume officers.
answer.evidence: Woodland Alliance — Daylight and Evening operations

answer.ruling: During Evening, Alliance may take up to its number of officers in operations, in any order and repetition. One Organize operation removes one Alliance warrior from an unsympathetic clearing, places sympathy there, and scores the uncovered VP. It costs no supporters and has no adjacency or Martial Law cost, but legal token placement is still required. Draw after operations: one card plus uncovered draw bonuses, then discard down to five.
answer.evidence: Woodland Alliance — Daylight and Evening operations

answer.ruling: Whenever a base is removed, discard supporters matching its clearing, including birds, and remove half the officers rounded up. If no bases remain, discard excess supporters down to five.

evidence: Woodland Alliance — Daylight and Evening operations

source_passages.quotation:
1. **Refresh:** First count tea **already face up on Refresh track**; flip two exhausted items face up per counted tea, then three more exhausted items. Tea refreshed during this step gives no extra refresh this step. Refreshing changes face, not damaged status.
2. **Slip (optional):** Move to an adjacent clearing or forest, exhausting **no boots**, even into hostile warriors. Ignore all effects preventing movement **out of** a clearing. **Forest adjacency for Slip:** a forest is adjacent to clearings touching it without crossing a printed path, and to forests separated by one printed path. On Winter, the river also divides forests as paths do.

- **Move:** Exhaust one boot, plus **one extra boot** if destination has any warriors of any Hostile faction (also for forced moves). Ignore rule. **Cannot enter a forest with this action; from a forest you may move only to an adjacent clearing.** Slip has the special free-boot exception.

1. If in forest, **Rest**: return all damaged items to Satchel and flip them face up; ready tea/coins/bags move to tracks if able. This does not refresh undamaged exhausted items.
2. **Always draw**, even after forest Rest: one card plus one per face-up coins on track.
3. Discard hand to five.
4. **Capacity, the last step of Evening after drawing and discarding:** Satchel **plus Damaged box** may contain **six items plus two per face-up bag on its track**. Track items do not count toward load. Permanently remove chosen Satchel/Damaged items until within limit. Do not check capacity immediately upon acquiring an item.

answer.ruling: At Birdsong, count tea already face up on the Refresh track; flip two exhausted items face up per such tea, then flip three more exhausted items. Tea refreshed during this step adds no refresh this step. This changes face, not damage status.

Optional Slip moves to an adjacent clearing or forest without exhausting boots, even into hostile warriors. Ignore effects that prevent movement out of a clearing. A forest is adjacent to clearings touching it without crossing a printed path and to forests separated by one printed path; Winter’s river also divides forests like paths.

answer.part: Normal Move and hostile destination cost
answer.ruling: For Daylight Move, exhaust one boot, plus one extra boot if the destination contains any warriors of any Hostile faction. This applies to forced moves too. Ignore rule. This action cannot enter a forest; from a forest it can move only to an adjacent clearing.

If in a forest, Rest returns all damaged items to Satchel and flips them face up; ready tea, coins and bags move to tracks if able. Rest does not refresh undamaged exhausted items. Always draw afterward, even after Rest: one card plus one per face-up coin on track. Then discard to five.

source_passages.quotation: - **Explore:** Exhaust torch in ruin's clearing. Take one hidden item face up into Satchel or track; score one VP if an item taken. Remove ruin when its last item is taken, freeing the building slot.

- **Quest (matching clearing only):** Choose a face-up quest matching clearing; exhaust its **two listed items**, put quest in play area completed. Choose either VP equal to matching completed quests **including this one**, or draw two cards. Draw replacement quest into public display. No cards are spent to pay a quest.
- **Repair:** Exhaust hammer; move one damaged item to Satchel **keeping current face**. Ready tea/coins/bags move to tracks if space.

answer.ruling: Exhaust a torch in the ruin’s clearing. Take one hidden item face up into Satchel or a track and score one VP if an item was taken. Remove the ruin when its last item is taken, freeing the building slot.

In a clearing matching a face-up quest, exhaust its two listed items and put the quest in your play area completed. Choose VP equal to your matching completed quests, including this one, or draw two cards. Draw a replacement quest into the public display. No cards pay the quest cost.
Exhaust a hammer and move one damaged item to Satchel, keeping its current face. If ready tea, coins or bags are repaired, move them to tracks if space allows.

source_passages.quotation: - **Aid:** Exhaust **one face-up, undamaged item of any type**, give a card matching your clearing to player with faction pieces there, even Hostile. May then take one item from their Crafted Items box face up into Satchel/track; no available item is required to Aid. **Only non-Hostile relationships can advance through Aid; a Hostile recipient stays Hostile.** Check relationship improvement below.

- **Strike:** Exhaust crossbow to remove one enemy warrior in clearing. Only if that enemy has no warriors there may you remove another of its faction pieces instead. Check hostility. Strike is not battle and gives no Infamy.

source_passages.section: Vagabond — Hostile and Infamy; Aid and hostility
source_passages.quotation:
- **Hostile:** Removing **one** warrior of a non-Hostile faction immediately moves marker to Hostile (except allied battle-loss rule above). **Infamy:** During battle on your own turn, score **one extra VP per hostile piece removed**, except warrior that first made faction Hostile. **Each hostile building/token removed in battle on your turn normally scores two VP: one removal VP plus one Infamy. A hostile warrior scores one Infamy, except the warrior that first caused Hostile status.** Infamy depends on whose turn it is, rather than which side attacks: no Infamy on another player's turn, and none from Strike. Hostile status requires extra boot for moves into hostile warriors, not merely buildings/tokens.
- Aid cannot move marker out of Hostile; it can still obtain a crafted item. Coalition with Hostile faction resets its marker to Indifferent.

answer.part: Hostility trigger and Aid cannot undo it
answer.ruling: Removing one warrior of a non-Hostile faction immediately moves its relationship marker to Hostile, except the special allied battle-loss rule. Aid cannot move a marker out of Hostile, though Aid can still obtain a crafted item.
answer.evidence: Vagabond — Hostile and Infamy; Aid and hostility

answer.ruling: During battle on the Vagabond’s own turn, score one extra VP per hostile piece removed, except the warrior that first made the faction Hostile. A hostile building or token normally yields two VP in that battle: one ordinary removal VP plus one Infamy; a hostile warrior yields one Infamy, except the warrior that first caused Hostile status. Infamy depends on whose turn it is, not which side attacks; it is not scored on another player’s turn or from Strike.
answer.evidence: Vagabond — Hostile and Infamy; Aid and hostility

answer.ruling: Strike exhausts a crossbow to remove one enemy warrior in the clearing. Only if that enemy has no warriors there may Strike remove another of its faction pieces instead. Check hostility; Strike is not battle and gives no Infamy.

evidence: Vagabond — Hostile and Infamy; Aid and hostility

source_passages.quotation: **Vagabond coalition (9.2.8):** Cannot activate normal dominance win. With **four or more players**, during own Daylight at **at least 10 VP**, activate dominance to coalition with another player **not already in coalition**, whose VP is lowest among players other than you (choose among ties). **An already-activated dominance player cannot be chosen:** they have no score marker on the track (publisher clarification in **FAQ & Rulings**). Compare eligible players still on the score track. Put your score marker on partner's faction board and stop scoring. If partner wins, you also win, including if partner later activates and wins through dominance. Coalition partners are not enemies. A Hostile partner becomes Indifferent. Coalition does not by itself grant Allied relationship powers.

source_passages.section: Vagabond — Hostility and coalition relationship effect
source_passages.quotation: - Aid cannot move marker out of Hostile; it can still obtain a crafted item. Coalition with Hostile faction resets its marker to Indifferent.

answer.part: Eligibility, timing, VP and partner selection
answer.ruling: Vagabond cannot activate a normal dominance win. With four or more players, during its own Daylight at at least 10 VP, it may activate dominance to coalition with a player not already in a coalition. The partner must have the lowest VP among all players other than Vagabond; Vagabond chooses among ties. A player who already activated dominance cannot be chosen because that player has no score marker on the track. Vagabond puts its score marker on the partner’s faction board and stops scoring.

The Vagabond wins if its partner wins, including if that partner later activates and wins through dominance. Coalition partners are not enemies. A Hostile partner becomes Indifferent. Coalition alone does not grant Allied relationship powers.
answer.evidence: Vagabond coalition; Vagabond — Hostility and coalition relationship effect

evidence: Vagabond — Hostility and coalition relationship effect

source_passages.quotation: - **Precedence:** Card overrides Law; Law overrides Learning to Play. Follow general and faction rules together when possible; if incompatible, faction rule wins. **Cannot is absolute** unless explicitly overridden. (1.1.)

answer.ruling: A card overrides the Law; the Law overrides Learning to Play. General and faction rules are used together where possible, and when they conflict the faction rule wins. “Cannot” is absolute unless explicitly overridden. An ordinary card does not override a Cannot unless it explicitly does so.

source_passages.quotation: Take turns clockwise: **Birdsong → Daylight → Evening**. “At start” effects precede all other phase effects; “at end” effects follow everything else in that phase, before next phase. Once the last step of a turn begins, no other actions are allowed except explicitly end-of-Evening/turn actions. An action, ability or persistent effect cannot be interrupted unless an effect explicitly permits it; a Marquise March's two moves are one compound action. If simultaneous effects have no clear order or decision maker, the player taking the turn chooses. For battle effects at the same timing, attacker chooses their order. (1.1.3, 1.4, 4.3.)

answer.ruling: When simultaneous effects have no clear order or decision maker, the player taking the turn chooses. For battle effects at the same timing, the attacker chooses their order.
No: a March’s two moves are one compound action and cannot be interrupted to spend a bird card or take another action.

source_passages.quotation: Take turns clockwise: **Birdsong → Daylight → Evening**. “At start” effects precede all other phase effects; “at end” effects follow everything else in that phase, before next phase. Once the last step of a turn begins, no other actions are allowed except explicitly end-of-Evening/turn actions. An action, ability or persistent effect cannot be interrupted unless an effect explicitly permits it; a Marquise March's two moves are one compound action. If simultaneous effects have no clear order or decision maker, the player taking the turn chooses. For battle effects at the same timing, attacker chooses their order. (1.1.3, 1.4, 4.3.)

answer.ruling: At-start effects happen before all other effects of that phase. At-end effects happen after all other effects in that phase, before the next phase.

answer.part: Actions after the last turn step begins
answer.ruling: Once the last step of a turn begins, no other actions are allowed except actions explicitly allowed at the end of Evening or the turn; ordinary Daylight actions cannot be taken then.

source_passages.section: Special Rules & Edge Cases — Information and agreements
source_passages.quotation: - Hand size is public, contents private: reveal/show only if explicitly instructed. Face-up piles may be searched/inspected; deck cannot. Agreements are non-binding; cards may be transferred only as instructed; actions require no consent. (1.2–3.)

answer.part: Information players may inspect or reveal
answer.ruling: Hand size is public but hand contents are private; reveal or show contents only if explicitly instructed. Face-up piles may be searched or inspected, but the deck may not.
answer.evidence: Special Rules & Edge Cases — Information and agreements

answer.ruling: Agreements are non-binding. Cards may be transferred only as instructed by the rules or an effect. Actions require no consent.
answer.evidence: Special Rules & Edge Cases — Information and agreements

evidence: Special Rules & Edge Cases — Information and agreements

source_passages.quotation: - **Cards:** Birds substitute for any non-bird suit, even for multiple same-suit payments. **If prompted to give or discard cards of a non-bird suit, you must treat your birds as that suit**; the instruction determines how many cards to give or discard. **Only a bird card can pay an explicit bird-card requirement; fox, rabbit and mouse cards cannot pay it.** Draw from shared deck top; when deck empties, immediately shuffle discard into new deck. (2.1.)

answer.ruling: Draw from the shared deck top. When the deck empties, immediately shuffle the discard pile into a new deck.

Bird cards substitute for any non-bird suit, including multiple same-suit payments. When instructed to give or discard cards of a non-bird suit, treat birds as that suit, following the instructed number of cards. But an explicit bird-card requirement can only be paid with a bird card; fox, rabbit and mouse cards cannot pay it.

source_passages.quotation: Removed faction pieces normally return to supply; tracked pieces return to the **rightmost empty track space**. Placement normally takes pieces from supply, or leftmost on a track. Items removed from the game are removed permanently. Pieces are finite: no proxies. When an instruction cannot place/take/remove all prompted pieces, **you must do the maximum possible and cannot voluntarily do fewer**; this never waives costs or prerequisites, nor the Eyrie's obligation to complete Decree actions. For simultaneous removal, remove all pieces before triggering removal effects. (1.5, G.20, G.24.)

answer.part: Shortage, proxies, maximum placement, costs and Decree
answer.ruling: Pieces are finite and proxies are not allowed. If an instruction prompts more placements than pieces available, place the maximum possible; you may not voluntarily place fewer. A shortage does not waive costs or prerequisites, and does not waive the Eyrie’s obligation to complete Decree actions.

source_passages.quotation:
6. **Deal hits:** Each hit removes one opposing piece. The side taking hits chooses its own removal order, but **all its warriors must be removed before its buildings/tokens**. It also chooses order of effects triggered by its pieces' removal. Both sides deal their counted hits; losing warriors does not retroactively change the rolled cap. Whoever removes an enemy building/token scores **one VP each**, even while defending and even outside battle. Vagabond takes hits as item damage instead.

Removed faction pieces normally return to supply; tracked pieces return to the **rightmost empty track space**. Placement normally takes pieces from supply, or leftmost on a track. Items removed from the game are removed permanently. Pieces are finite: no proxies. When an instruction cannot place/take/remove all prompted pieces, **you must do the maximum possible and cannot voluntarily do fewer**; this never waives costs or prerequisites, nor the Eyrie's obligation to complete Decree actions. For simultaneous removal, remove all pieces before triggering removal effects. (1.5, G.20, G.24.)

answer.part: Where pieces come from and go
answer.ruling: Placements normally take pieces from supply or from the leftmost track space. Removed faction pieces normally return to supply, while tracked pieces return to the rightmost empty track space. Removed items are permanently removed from the game.
When removals are simultaneous, remove all pieces before triggering effects caused by their removal.

source_passages.quotation: - **Force:** Resolve forced actions as if affected player chose them, retaining their abilities and restrictions. A player forced to battle makes its battle decisions. (1.5.5.)

answer.ruling: Resolve a forced action as if the affected player chose it, so that player retains their own abilities and restrictions. If forced to battle, that player makes the battle decisions.

source_passages.quotation: **Keep:** Only Marquise may **place** pieces in its clearing; other players may **move** pieces into it. The keep cannot be placed again if removed. **Field Hospitals:** Whenever any number of Marquise warriors are removed from a clearing, Marquise may spend one card matching that clearing to place those warriors in the keep clearing instead of supply. This can apply outside battle. Without a keep there is no destination for hospitals. See **FAQ & Rulings** for Hospitals during an ambush at the Keep.

source_passages.section: Special Rules & Edge Cases — Place/remove/replace and swap
source_passages.quotation: - **Place/remove/replace:** Place normally from supply/leftmost track; remove normally to supply/rightmost **empty** track space, items permanently. Replace requires both removal and placement possible; the keep's placement ban cannot be bypassed by replacing an enemy piece. Swap ignores move/place restrictions. Spending a card means discarding it, with dominance's special destination. (G.5, G.20, G.23–24, G.31, G.33.)

answer.part: Replacing a piece in the Keep clearing
answer.ruling: No. Only Marquise may place pieces in its Keep clearing. Replacement requires that both removal and placement be possible, and cannot bypass the Keep’s placement ban. Other players may move pieces into the Keep clearing.
answer.evidence: Marquise de Cat — Keep placement; Special Rules & Edge Cases — Place/remove/replace and swap

answer.part: Swap compared with move or place
answer.ruling: A swap ignores move and place restrictions; it is not governed by those restrictions as a move or placement would be.
answer.evidence: Special Rules & Edge Cases — Place/remove/replace and swap

evidence: Special Rules & Edge Cases — Place/remove/replace and swap

source_passages.quotation: **30 VP:** First to 30 wins immediately, on any player's turn. If multiple reach 30 simultaneously, tied player closest clockwise to current player wins, including current player. Removing enemy buildings/tokens gives one VP each regardless of phase or whether attacker/defender. Crafting items scores printed VP except Eyrie's Disdain. Faction scoring is described above. (3.1–2.)

answer.ruling: If multiple players reach 30 VP simultaneously, the tied player closest clockwise to the current player wins; the current player is included in this order.

source_passages.quotation: Clearings have fox, rabbit or mouse suit and limited building slots. Buildings require open slots; tokens do not occupy these. Ruins block their slots and can be removed only when explicitly allowed. A forest is enclosed by printed paths and clearings; it is adjacent to clearings touching it without crossing a printed path and to forests separated by just one printed path. Winter's river also divides forests. (2.2–2.4, M.1–2.)

1. Choose factions; determine starting player and seating randomly. Take faction boards and their listed pieces. Use Fall or Winter. Fall has no special rules; on Winter, the river divides forests just as printed paths do. Rivers are otherwise not paths.

2. **Slip (optional):** Move to an adjacent clearing or forest, exhausting **no boots**, even into hostile warriors. Ignore all effects preventing movement **out of** a clearing. **Forest adjacency for Slip:** a forest is adjacent to clearings touching it without crossing a printed path, and to forests separated by one printed path. On Winter, the river also divides forests as paths do.

answer.part: Forest adjacency and Winter river for Slip
answer.ruling: For Slip, a forest is adjacent to clearings touching it without crossing a printed path, and to forests separated by one printed path. On Winter, the river also divides forests like paths do.
answer.evidence: Map and forest rules; Vagabond — Slip

answer.ruling: Fall has no special rules.

source_passages.quotation: **Marquise setup (6.3):** Supply 25 warriors and 8 wood. Put keep in any corner (starting clearing). Put one warrior in every clearing except the diagonally opposite corner. Place one sawmill, workshop and recruiter among the keep clearing and adjacent clearings, in any combination respecting slots. Put the remaining five buildings of each type on their tracks from right to left, leaving leftmost space empty.

answer.ruling: Supply 25 warriors and 8 wood. Put the Keep in any corner clearing, then put one warrior in every clearing except the diagonally opposite corner. Place one sawmill, one workshop and one recruiter among the Keep clearing and its adjacent clearings, in any combination that respects building slots. Put the remaining five buildings of each type on their tracks from right to left, leaving each track’s leftmost space empty.

source_passages.quotation: **Eyrie setup (7.3):** Supply 20 warriors. Put one roost and six warriors in a corner that is not another player's starting corner, diagonally opposite a starting corner if possible. Choose a leader; keep others face up nearby. Tuck the two bird Loyal Viziers into the columns listed on that leader. Fill roost track with the other six roosts from right to left.

answer.part: Eyrie warriors, roost, leader, Viziers and track
answer.ruling: Supply 20 warriors. Put one roost and six warriors in a corner that is not another player’s starting corner, diagonally opposite a starting corner if possible. Choose a leader and keep the others face up nearby. Tuck the two bird Loyal Viziers into the columns listed for that leader. Put the other six roosts on the roost track from right to left.

source_passages.quotation: **Alliance setup (8.3):** Supply 10 warriors. Put the three bases in their matching board spaces and ten sympathy on its track. Draw **three additional cards** face down into Supporters; these are separate from your three-card hand. Start with no map pieces or officers.

answer.part: Alliance supply, board pieces, cards and map
answer.ruling: Supply 10 warriors. Put the three bases in their matching board spaces and ten sympathy on the sympathy track. Put three additional cards face down in Supporters, separate from the three-card hand. The Alliance starts with no map pieces and no officers.

source_passages.quotation: **Vagabond setup (9.3):** Choose Thief, Tinker or Ranger; place pawn in any forest. Shuffle quests and display three face up. Hide one each of the **R-marked bag, boot, hammer and sword** beneath the four ruins: assemble and shuffle the four stacks and return each to an empty R slot so identities are hidden. Take S-marked starting items listed on character: tea, coins and bags go face up on matching tracks, other items face up in Satchel; return unused S items to box. Place each other faction's relationship marker at Indifferent.

answer.part: Pawn, quests, relationships and marked starting items
answer.ruling: Choose Thief, Tinker or Ranger and place the pawn in any forest. Shuffle the quests and display three face up. Take the S-marked starting items listed for the chosen character: tea, coins and bags go face up on matching tracks; other starting items go face up in Satchel; return unused S-marked items to the box. Set each other faction’s relationship marker to Indifferent.

source_passages.quotation: **Recommended faction mix (5.2):** Reach should total at least 17 for two players, 18 for three, 21 for four. Base reach: Marquise 10, Eyrie 7, Vagabond 5, Alliance 3. The Law allows adventurous groups to use any mix totaling at least 17.

answer.part: Reach totals and base faction values
answer.ruling: Recommended minimum total Reach is 17 for two players, 18 for three, and 21 for four. Base values are Marquise 10, Eyrie 7, Vagabond 5, and Alliance 3. The Law also allows adventurous groups to use any mix totaling at least 17.

source_passages.quotation:
**Wood production:** Birdsong places one wood per sawmill in its clearing. During Daylight, each Overwork action spends a card matching a sawmill clearing to place one wood there. Both methods draw from the same finite supply of eight wood tokens.

**Birdsong:** Place one wood at each sawmill (one per sawmill if multiple share a clearing), limited by eight wood supply.
**Evening:** Draw one card plus one per uncovered draw bonus; discard hand down to five.

answer.ruling: At Birdsong, place one wood at each sawmill, one per sawmill even if several share a clearing. At Daylight, each Overwork action spends a card matching a sawmill’s clearing to place one wood there. Both production methods use the finite supply of eight wood tokens, so production is limited by the wood available.
In Evening, draw one card plus one per uncovered draw bonus, then discard down to five cards.

source_passages.quotation: - **Recruit:** One warrior at **each recruiter**; only **once per turn**. If supply cannot fill all recruiters, place maximum available, choosing among eligible recruiters.

answer.ruling: Recruit places one warrior at each recruiter, and may be used only once per turn. If supply cannot fill all recruiters, place the maximum available and choose among eligible recruiters where to place them.

source_passages.quotation: - Immediate effect (paper box): resolve, then discard the **crafting card**. An item card requires the corresponding **item token** in the map supply, or it cannot be crafted. Take the item token into Crafted Items and score the VP printed on the card, subject to Eyrie exception. The item token stays; the crafting card is discarded. Ordinary factions do not exhaust crafted items as Vagabond does.

**Lords of the Forest:** Win ties for rule if at least one Eyrie piece there. **Disdain for Trade:** Crafted items score only **one VP instead of printed VP** (other extra crafting-point effects still apply). Builder ignores Disdain.

answer.part: Eyrie crafted item VP and other crafting points
answer.ruling: An item card requires its corresponding item token in map supply to craft; on a successful craft, take the item token and score the VP printed on the card subject to the Eyrie exception. Eyrie’s Disdain for Trade makes a crafted item score one VP instead of its printed VP, but other extra crafting-point effects still apply. The Builder leader ignores Disdain for Trade.
answer.evidence: Crafted item effect; Eyrie Disdain and Builder ability

Viziers are in Recruit and Battle. Each Recruit must place two warriors instead of one.
Viziers are in Move and Battle. Commander gets one extra hit as attacker.
Viziers are in Move and Build. When removing at least one enemy building or token in battle, Despot scores one extra VP in addition to normal removal points.

source_passages.quotation: | Recruit | Clearing with a roost | Place **one warrior at one chosen roost** there; Charismatic must instead place **two warriors** there |

- **Charismatic and a supply shortage:** When a legal Decree Recruit requires two warriors but only one remains in supply, place that warrior first. Then enter Turmoil because the required two were not placed. Maximum-possible placement does not fulfill an incomplete Decree action. (FAQ under 7.7 and 7.8.2; Law 1.5.4.)

source_passages.quotation: **Guerrilla War:** When Alliance defends, Alliance uses higher die and attacker lower; warrior caps still apply. **Supporters** are a separate face-down stack, inspectable by Alliance. They can be spent only for suit; they do not count as hand cards or toward hand limit. With no bases on map, maximum **five supporters**; incoming cards beyond capacity are discarded. With any base, unlimited supporters.

answer.part: Dice and warrior cap when Alliance defends
answer.ruling: When Alliance defends, Alliance uses the higher die and the attacker uses the lower die. Warrior caps on rolled hits still apply.

source_passages.quotation: **Guerrilla War:** When Alliance defends, Alliance uses higher die and attacker lower; warrior caps still apply. **Supporters** are a separate face-down stack, inspectable by Alliance. They can be spent only for suit; they do not count as hand cards or toward hand limit. With no bases on map, maximum **five supporters**; incoming cards beyond capacity are discarded. With any base, unlimited supporters.
- **Craft** from hand with sympathy.

answer.ruling: Supporters are a separate face-down stack that Alliance may inspect. They can be spent only for suit, not as crafting cards; Alliance crafts from hand. Supporters are not hand cards and do not count toward the hand limit.
answer.evidence: Woodland Alliance — Supporters; Woodland Alliance — Daylight Craft

source_passages.quotation: **Birdsong:** Both Revolt and Spread Sympathy take place **during Birdsong**. Complete **all Revolts before starting any Spread Sympathy**; each may be performed any number of times. **For both actions, every supporter spent must match the target clearing; birds are wild.** Once spreading starts, you cannot return to Revolt this Birdsong, so newly spread sympathy cannot support a same-Birdsong Revolt:

answer.part: Spread then Revolt during the same Birdsong
answer.ruling: No. Alliance must complete all Revolts before beginning Spread Sympathy. Once spreading starts, it cannot return to Revolt that Birdsong, so sympathy newly spread in that phase cannot support a same-Birdsong Revolt.

source_passages.section: Woodland Alliance — Spread Sympathy Martial Law
source_passages.quotation: - **Spread Sympathy:** Choose unsympathetic clearing adjacent by path to sympathy; if no sympathy anywhere, choose any clearing. Spend matching supporters shown above next sympathy token. **Martial Law:** add one matching supporter if chosen clearing has at least three warriors of **one other player**. Place token and score uncovered space. Only one sympathy per clearing. Keep's placement ban still applies.

Organize spends no supporters and has no sympathy-adjacency requirement or Martial Law cost; it still needs legal token placement. **After operations**, draw one card plus one per uncovered draw bonus, then discard hand down to five.

answer.part: Martial Law with two different players each having two warriors
answer.ruling: No. Spread Sympathy adds the Martial Law supporter only when the chosen clearing has at least three warriors belonging to one other player. Two warriors from each of two players do not meet that threshold.
answer.evidence: Woodland Alliance — Spread Sympathy Martial Law

answer.ruling: No Martial Law supporter is added for Organize: Organize has no Martial Law cost or sympathy-adjacency requirement, and spends no supporters. Legal sympathy token placement is still required.

evidence: Woodland Alliance — Spread Sympathy Martial Law

source_passages.quotation: **Outrage:** Each time another player **removes sympathy** or **moves any warriors into a sympathetic clearing**, that player adds one matching hand card (birds count) to Supporters. Moving a group costs one card per affected move, rather than one per warrior. If no matching cards including birds, show hand to Alliance, then Alliance draws one deck card into Supporters. **If Supporters is full, discard the incoming Outrage card; payment or the no-match draw still occurs.** Merely battling there is no trigger unless sympathy is removed; placing warriors there and moving only Vagabond pawn do not trigger it.

source_passages.section: FAQ & Rulings — Allied movement and Outrage
source_passages.quotation: - **Allied movement and Outrage:** Forcing Allied **Woodland Alliance** warriors to accompany the Vagabond into sympathy causes **no Outrage**: resolve the move as the Alliance moving its own warriors. Warriors of another Allied faction entering sympathy do trigger Outrage for that moving faction, which pays from its own hand under the normal Outrage procedure. The Vagabond pawn alone causes no warrior-entry Outrage; removing sympathy still triggers it. (FAQ under 8.2.6 and 9.2.9; Law 1.5.5, 8.2.6.)

answer.part: Placing warriors and moving only Vagabond pawn
answer.ruling: Neither placing warriors in a sympathetic clearing nor moving only the Vagabond pawn there triggers Outrage. Outrage triggers when another player moves warriors into a sympathetic clearing or removes sympathy.

Forcing Allied Woodland Alliance warriors into sympathy with the Vagabond causes no Outrage: resolve the move as if the Alliance moved its own warriors. Warriors of another Allied faction entering sympathy do trigger Outrage for that moving faction, which pays from its own hand under normal Outrage rules.
answer.evidence: FAQ & Rulings — Allied movement and Outrage

source_passages.quotation:
**Evening:** The four military operations are **Move, Battle, Recruit and Organize**. Take **up to your number of officers** in operations, in any order and repetition. Officers stay on the board; taking an operation does not consume an officer. After operations, draw one card plus one per uncovered draw bonus, then discard hand down to five.

| Military operation | Procedure for one operation |
|---|---|
| Move | Take one move using normal movement rules |
| Battle | Initiate one battle |
| Recruit | Place one warrior at one clearing with a base |
| Organize | Remove one Alliance warrior from an unsympathetic clearing; place sympathy there; score the uncovered VP |

Organize spends no supporters and has no sympathy-adjacency requirement or Martial Law cost; it still needs legal token placement. **After operations**, draw one card plus one per uncovered draw bonus, then discard hand down to five.

answer.ruling: Alliance may take the four military operations—Move, Battle, Recruit and Organize—in any order and with repetition, up to its number of officers. Officers remain on the board and operations do not consume them. One operation is one Move under normal rules; one initiated Battle; one Recruit placing one warrior at one clearing with a base; or one Organize removing one Alliance warrior from an unsympathetic clearing, placing sympathy there and scoring the uncovered VP. Organize spends no supporters and has no adjacency or Martial Law cost, but requires legal token placement.
After operations, draw one card plus one per uncovered draw bonus, then discard hand down to five.

source_passages.quotation: **Pawn and items:** Pawn is not a warrior, cannot rule or block rule, and cannot be removed. An enemy effect removing **all enemy pieces** from its clearing instead damages **three items**. Items may be face up (ready) or face down (exhausted), and independently undamaged or damaged. To exhaust for an action, choose a face-up **undamaged** item and flip it down. Damaged items cannot pay actions.

- **Revolt:** Choose sympathetic clearing without a base, matching a base still on your board. Spend **two matching supporters**. **Remove all enemy pieces there and score one VP per enemy building/token removed**; then place matching base. Place warriors there equal to number of sympathetic clearings matching the base's printed suit (including revolt clearing), and one warrior in Officers box. Score normal VP for removed enemy buildings/tokens. Resolve the effect even if a prompted placement cannot be completed: place the maximum possible, without adding a base-placement prerequisite. Enemy Vagabond damages three items instead of being removed.

answer.part: Vagabond pawn in a remove-all-pieces effect or Revolt
answer.ruling: The Vagabond pawn cannot be removed. When an enemy effect removes all enemy pieces from its clearing, instead damage three Vagabond items. Specifically during Revolt, the enemy Vagabond damages three items instead of being removed.
answer.evidence: Vagabond — Pawn and items; Woodland Alliance — Revolt

source_passages.quotation: - **Battle:** Exhaust one sword to initiate. Maximum rolled hits, attacking or defending, equals **all undamaged swords in Satchel, face up or face down**. As defender you are defenseless only with no undamaged swords. Take hits as item damage.

Face-up tea/coins/bags in Satchel immediately move to empty matching track space if possible; each track holds at most three of its type. Exhausting an item on track sends it to Satchel. Boots/swords/crossbows/torch/hammers are gained face up in Satchel. Damaging an item sends it to Damaged box **without changing its face**. One hit damages one undamaged item of your choice; ignore excess hits when none remain.

answer.ruling: Vagabond’s maximum rolled hits, as attacker or defender, equal all undamaged swords in Satchel, whether face up or face down; exhausted undamaged swords count. As defender, Vagabond is defenseless only if it has no undamaged swords.
Vagabond takes hits as item damage: each hit damages one undamaged item of its choice. If no undamaged items remain, excess hits are ignored.

source_passages.quotation:
**Pawn and items:** Pawn is not a warrior, cannot rule or block rule, and cannot be removed. An enemy effect removing **all enemy pieces** from its clearing instead damages **three items**. Items may be face up (ready) or face down (exhausted), and independently undamaged or damaged. To exhaust for an action, choose a face-up **undamaged** item and flip it down. Damaged items cannot pay actions.

Face-up tea/coins/bags in Satchel immediately move to empty matching track space if possible; each track holds at most three of its type. Exhausting an item on track sends it to Satchel. Boots/swords/crossbows/torch/hammers are gained face up in Satchel. Damaging an item sends it to Damaged box **without changing its face**. One hit damages one undamaged item of your choice; ignore excess hits when none remain.
- **Repair:** Exhaust hammer; move one damaged item to Satchel **keeping current face**. Ready tea/coins/bags move to tracks if space.

answer.part: Tea, coins and bags moving to/from tracks and capacity
answer.ruling: Face-up tea, coins and bags in Satchel immediately move to their matching track if a space is available; each track holds at most three of that item type. When a track item is exhausted, it moves to Satchel. When a hammer repairs a damaged item, it returns to Satchel keeping its face; ready tea, coins or bags then move to tracks if space is available.

answer.part: Damaged face-up items and action cost
answer.ruling: Face-up/face-down status and damaged/undamaged status are independent. To exhaust an item for an action, it must be face up and undamaged; damaged items cannot pay actions, even when face up. Damage does not change an item’s face.
